**Test Image Analysis:**
- Young corn leaves showing yellowing and pale coloration
- Some leaves appear to have lighter, yellowish tissue alternating with greener areas
- Linear patterns visible on some leaves suggesting striping
- Overall pale/chlorotic appearance suggesting a systemic viral or nutrient condition

Let me compare with reference images for the top candidates.

The Maize_dwarf_mosaic_virus reference stands out with clear **light green to yellow parallel streaks along leaf veins** - this matches the striping pattern I see in the test image. Let me view two more references to confirm.

**Reference Comparison Summary:**

After reviewing 6 reference images, **Maize_dwarf_mosaic_virus** is the strongest match:

| Feature | Test Image | MDMV Reference | Match? |
|---------|-----------|-----------------|--------|
| Striping pattern | Clear parallel light green/yellow stripes | Light green to yellow streaks along veins | ✓ Strong |
| Plant stage | Young, early symptoms | Early striping visible | ✓ |
| Overall color | Pale/chlorotic with stripes | Pale with yellow-green stripes | ✓ |
| Downy mildew comparison | Stripes less white, less shredding | White stripes, more tissue damage | ✗ |
| Corn Stunt comparison | No severe stunting/reddening | Severe stunting, purplish coloration | ✗ |

The test image displays the **pathognomonic light green to yellow parallel striping along leaf veins** that is diagnostic for Maize dwarf mosaic virus in its early stage.
